answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie each agent identity to a costly stake that gets slashed when peers prove it submitted fabricated work. An operator spinning up thousands of agents must lock capital for each one, which makes mass fake identities expensive. New identities also start with little voting weight, so they cannot vouch for each other in a spiral of fake endorsements. Attestations from established peers count more, and a steady pulse of honest activity earns rewards. Any cluster acting in lockstep, like a jetty of identical answers, gets flagged.
